prompts: Read through this repository (every package, docs/DESIGN.md and the README) and reply with a short summary of how a request flows from main to the store, naming the files involved.

In the config package, add a Timeout field of type time.Duration to Config, read from the environment variable SVC_TIMEOUT (a Go duration string such as 5s; default 5s; an invalid value must make Load return an error). Add tests for the default and for an invalid value.
Make the HTTP server use the timeout you just added as both ReadTimeout and WriteTimeout instead of the hard-coded values.
Add a GET /healthz endpoint that returns JSON {"status":"ok","timeout":"<the configured timeout, e.g. 5s>"}. Add a server test for it.

Rename the in-memory store type from MemStore to MemoryStore everywhere it appears: code, tests, comments, docs/DESIGN.md and the README (the constructor becomes NewMemoryStore). Nothing may still say MemStore.
Add a '## Configuration' section to the README that lists every environment variable the service reads, with its default, including the variable you added earlier in this session for the timeout.
Run go vet ./... and go test ./... and fix anything that fails. When everything passes, reply with exactly the name of the timeout environment variable you added and nothing else.

files.README.md:
# svc

A small items API: create, fetch, list (optionally by tag) and delete items
held in an in-memory store (`store.MemStore`).

## Running

```
make build
SVC_ADDR=:8080 ./bin/svc
```

## Endpoints

| method | path | notes |
|---|---|---|
| GET | /items | list, `?tag=` filters |
| POST | /items | JSON body `{"id","name","tags"}` |
| GET | /items/{id} | one item |
| DELETE | /items/{id} | remove |

See `docs/DESIGN.md` for how the packages fit together.
files.docs/DESIGN.md:
# Design notes

## Packages

- `config` reads the environment once at start-up and validates it. Every
  knob has a default in `config.Defaults`; `Load` never reads the
  environment twice, and nothing else in the service touches `os.Getenv`.
- `store` defines the `Store` interface and its only implementation,
  `MemStore`, a mutex-guarded map. Items are copied in and out, so callers
  cannot mutate stored state through a returned value.
- `server` builds the HTTP mux over a `Store`. Handlers are methods on
  `Server` so they share the store and logger without globals. `HTTPServer`
  applies the listen address and the read/write timeouts.
- `cmd/svc` is the only `main`: load config, make a store, serve.

## Request flow

1. `main` calls `config.Load`, fails fast on a bad environment.
2. `main` makes a `MemStore` and hands it with the config to `server.New`.
3. `Server.Handler` routes by method and path (Go 1.22 patterns); the
   `logged` middleware wraps the mux and records one line per request when
   the log level is `info` or `debug`.
4. A handler decodes the request, calls the store, and writes JSON with
   `writeJSON`/`writeError`. Store errors map to HTTP status: `ErrExists`
   is 409, `ErrNotFound` is 404, anything else is 500.

## Rules we keep

- The store interface stays small; add methods only with a caller.
- Handlers never return Go errors to clients verbatim except in the
  `error` field of the JSON body.
- Timeouts belong on the `http.Server`, not on individual handlers.
- Tests use `httptest` against `Handler()`; nothing binds a real port.

## Future

- A file-backed store behind `SVC_DB` (the variable is read but unused).
- Pagination on `GET /items` once lists get long.
- A health endpoint for load balancers.
